site.title: Acerola
site.description: A family of apps to look after your media library: read, watch and track what you consume, with the data on your machine or your own server.
site.footer: Open source under MPL-2.0 · acerola-brand standard

hero.title: Your media, your way
hero.lead: Read, watch and track what you consume, with the data on your machine or your own server. No cloud of ours, no account.

apps.title: One app for each part
apps.lead: Each app lives in its own repository, with its own docs and downloads. All of them follow the same brand and the same standard.

principles.title: What holds in every app
principles.lead: The direction every Acerola project follows, from the first commit to the deploy.

selfhost.title: Self-host first
selfhost.text: Each app runs on your machine or your server. The sync server, the reader relay and the sites come up with a compose file.

data.title: Your data stays with you
data.text: Library, progress and history live on your devices. When they need to travel, they go straight between them.

p2p.title: P2P or local network
p2p.text: Devices find each other and sync over the local network or P2P (iroh), with a relay only to get through NAT.

brand.title: One brand, one standard
brand.text: Every app follows the same design system and the same project standard, from acerola-brand.

open.title: Open source
open.text: Everything under MPL-2.0: read it, run it and contribute.

ideas.title: What comes next
ideas.lead: Nothing here is a promise: it is the direction the projects should take.

tmdb.title: Sync beyond anime and manga
tmdb.text: Track movies and series through TMDB and maybe Letterboxd. TMDB has an open API; Letterboxd doesn't, so it may be list import.

video.title: acerola-video
video.text: The reader's counterpart for video: your own library, synced progress and the same self-host and P2P principles.

platforms.title: Reader and video on every platform
platforms.text: Web, desktop and Android. The desktop becomes the library's agent; web-only users get a light agent, and everything talks over P2P or the local network.

docs.title: Docs for every project
docs.text: Each project with its own documentation, linked from here, and the design system in a single Storybook.

reader.name: Acerola Reader
reader.lead: Your comic and manga library on desktop and Android, synced straight between your own devices over P2P. No cloud, no account and no server to trust.

features.library: Local CBZ and CBR library, with covers, chapters and reading history.
features.sync: Progress synced between desktop and Android, straight between the devices.
features.relay: Off the same network, a relay gets through NAT with no open ports.
features.open: Desktop in Tauri + Svelte, Android in Kotlin + Compose, P2P in Rust.

sync.name: Acerola Sync
sync.tagline: Your AniList list, ticked off on its own.
sync.lead: A browser extension recognizes the open episode or chapter, and a Rust server of your own mirrors your AniList list and keeps everything in sync, anime and manga.

features.tracking: Marks the chapter after a few seconds on the page and the episode once the video passes 85%.
features.sites: Sakura Mangás, MangaDex, Crunchyroll, Netflix and any site you add by its URL.
features.mirror: Screens read from the Postgres mirror; AniList is only called to write and sync.
features.notify: New episode alerts, the title's page and where to watch or read.

brand.name: Acerola Brand
brand.tagline: The brand and the standard of every Acerola project.
brand.lead: Colors, typography, components, icon and mascot, published as a brand book and as files, plus the project standard every Acerola repository follows.

features.tokens: Color, shape and shadow tokens for Tailwind, plain CSS and Android.
features.components: .ac-* components, app screens, error screen and a sample site.
features.standard: Project standard: structure, i18n, git, hooks, workflows and license.
features.kit: A kit to start a project, with the skills and the checkers.

badRequest.title: Something in the request was off
badRequest.text: The address or the data sent came in a shape we don't understand. Check it and start over from the home page.

unauthorized.title: Sign in to continue
unauthorized.text: This page is only for signed-in accounts. Sign in and come back here.

forbidden.title: This page isn't for you
forbidden.text: Your account has no access to this. If you think it should, talk to whoever runs the app.

notFound.title: Page not found
notFound.text: The address may have changed or never existed. Go back to the start and take it from there.

timeout.title: That took too long
timeout.text: The answer didn't arrive in time. Try again in a moment.

tooMany.title: Easy, too many requests
tooMany.text: Too many requests in a short time. Wait a minute and try again.

server.title: Something broke on our side
server.text: The error was ours, not yours. Try again; if it keeps happening, come back later.

unavailable.title: Down for a moment
unavailable.text: The service is under maintenance or overloaded. Try again in a few minutes.

offline.title: You're offline
offline.text: Check your Wi-Fi or mobile data and try again.

unknown.title: Something went wrong
unknown.text: We're not sure what happened. Try again; if it keeps happening, go back to the start.
